// diagnostic

E0080

A braced callable with a non-unit success result needs `->` before its body.

What

A braced callable with a non-unit success result needs `->` before its body.

Why

The body arrow marks a declared success value; unit and unit-fallible callables keep bare braces.

Fix

Write `fn name(...) Type -> { ... }`; keep `fn name(...) { ... }` and `fn name(...) ! { ... }` bare.

Worked example

First UI snapshot mentioning E0080: tests/ui/foreign_declaration_binding.stderr.

Error [E0003]: `fun` is a function declaration keyword; Jet writes `fn`
  --> tests/ui/foreign_declaration_binding.jet:3:1
    |
  3 | fun add(left: Int, right: Int) -> Int {
    | ^^^
 Why: Jet uses one function declaration spelling so every declaration has one shape
 Fix: replace `fun` with `fn`
More: jet-lang.dev/e/E0003

Error [E0068]: this callable uses the retired result-arrow shape.
  --> tests/ui/foreign_declaration_binding.jet:3:32
    |
  3 | fun add(left: Int, right: Int) -> Int {
    |                                ^^
 Why: a return type sits after the parameter list, and `->` introduces the body; an effect ceiling follows the return type
 Fix: write `fn name(...) Type -> body`, or `fn name(...) Type -[Effects]> { … }`
More: jet-lang.dev/e/E0068

Error [E0003]: `var` is a foreign binding keyword; Jet writes `:=`
  --> tests/ui/foreign_declaration_binding.jet:20:5
    |
 20 |     var count: Int = 1
    |     ^^^
 Why: Jet puts binding mutability on `:=` or `::`, not on a declaration keyword
 Fix: write `name := value`

Error [E0003]: expected a call, binding, assignment, or `return`, found the keyword `const`
  --> tests/ui/foreign_declaration_binding.jet:22:5

    |     ^^^^^
 Why: inside a function body, write a call, binding, assignment, or `return`
 Fix: e.g. print("hello") or x :: 1
